title: Using Data Analysis to Spot Gaps in Maternal and Child Healthcare Service Delivery
short_description: Maternal and child health (MCH) tenders from Assam's e-procurement portal, 2019-2025, classified by scheme and geotagged to districts, to see where public MCH spending goes and how it relates to infant mortality.
question_it_answers: Where, on what, and through which departments and schemes does Assam spend public procurement money on maternal and child health, and does that line up with district health needs?

superset_dashboard.title: Linking Public Spending to Maternal and Child Health Outcomes in Assam

coverage.spatial: Assam, India; district level (35 districts as of the 2024-11 boundaries)

temporal.note: The '2019 to 2025' in titles is the period when results came out. Some tenders were first published in Dec 2017 and 2018.

coverage.temporal_unit: month (results batch); contract date for individual tenders
coverage.population: MCH-related tenders published on assamtenders.gov.in. Tenders not on the portal are not included; the use case page says only about 20% of Assam's tenders are published.

methodology_summary: Scrape monthly tender results from assamtenders.gov.in (TENDERS/scripts/scraper).
Flag MCH tenders with keyword rules on title, reference and work description; exclude veterinary and animal husbandry (TENDERS/scripts/mch_tenders.py).
Tag schemes by pattern matching (same script).
Assign a district from place names in the reference, title and location fields; mark CONFLICT when fields disagree (TENDERS/scripts/geocode_district.py).

published_findings._provenance: From the DataSpace use case narrative (2020-2023 analysis). Quote as the use case's findings, not as figures computed by the engine. Recompute from data where possible.

items.finding: Procurement shifted from NHM-led programme purchases in 2021 to infrastructure procurement by Public Works (Building and NH) and Health and Family Welfare in 2022-23.
Tenders were concentrated under NHM and SOPD; LAQSHYA, RCH and MSDP saw limited activity.
items.caveat: In the current tagging, LAQSHYA is the second most common scheme tag (28 tenders, all also tagged NHM; NHM has 49), because generic labour-room phrases match it. The finding and the data disagree; say so if asked.

items.finding: Dibrugarh, Jorhat and Kamrup Metro have higher IMR, although Kamrup Metro has some of the highest procurement spending, driven by a few large infrastructure projects.
Bongaigaon and Dhemaji received modest tender values but show better IMR.
Higher spending alone does not guarantee better health indicators; efficiency, relevance and local delivery capacity matter.
Only about 20% of Assam's tenders are published.
Contract award information is delayed by about 250 days on average against a 30-day disclosure rule.
items.caveat: Not the same as days_publish_to_contract in views.sql.

items.finding: Location fields, scheme names and work categories are inconsistent, which makes linking spending to interventions hard.

intended_users: NHM and Health Department officials planning district MCH infrastructure
Finance and planning officials linking spending to outcomes
CSOs and journalists tracking public MCH spending
limitations: Only tenders published on the state portal; total spending is understated.

19 of 59 awarded tenders (mostly goods: drugs, equipment, kits) record ₹0, ₹1 or a unit rate instead of the contract value, so goods and Health and Family Welfare spending are large undercounts (awarded_value_suspect in views.sql).
MCH classification is keyword based; it misses tenders with vague titles and may include weak matches.
13 tenders have no district and 3 have conflicting districts.
Scheme tags are pattern matches, not official scheme codes; CHD_SCHEME is a known false positive.
One tender (GMCH 500-bed Mother and Child Hospital, ₹214 crore) is about 80% of total awarded value; totals, trends and district rankings shift a lot with or without it.
Counts per district and per year are small (often 1-5 tenders).

sensitivity.personal_data: bidder_name includes some individual contractors. It is public procurement information, but do not rank, profile or make claims about named individuals. Aggregate by department, scheme or district instead.
sensitivity.framing: Do not suggest wrongdoing from single-bid tenders, rejections or delays.
